name: Holt-Oram Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of congenital upper limb malformations including radial ray defects
Presence of congenital heart defects, especially atrial septal defect or ventricular septal defect
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the TBX5 gene
Family history of Holt-Oram syndrome or related cardiac and limb anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital upper limb malformations and congenital heart defects, with or without TBX5 mutation confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for TBX5 mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical features are definitive

common.symptomName: Shortened forearm bones (radius or ulna hypoplasia)
Clubbing or malformation of carpal bones

occasional.symptomName: Reduced range of motion in upper limbs

imaging: X-ray showing radial ray defects and carpal bone abnormalities
Echocardiogram demonstrating septal defects and valvular abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in TBX5 gene detected by molecular genetic testing
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: No congenital heart defects typical of Holt-Oram syndrome
Multiple congenital anomalies including vertebral, anal, cardiac, tracheoesophageal, renal, and limb defects
Limb anomalies less specific to radial ray defects

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects causing heart failure
Progressive conduction abnormalities leading to syncope or sudden cardiac death
Severe upper limb malformations impairing function
references: Basson CT, et al. Mutations in human TBX5 cause limb and cardiac malformation in Holt-Oram syndrome. Nat Genet. 1997.
Bruneau BG. The developmental genetics of congenital heart disease. Nature. 2008.
